sources.outcomes: Limited evidence that exercise does not improve long-term patient-reported outcomes; this is not evidence of short-term harm.
sources.uncertainty: Recommendation pages/indexed passages inspected; not complete full guideline inspection. No maximum load/wrist-angle prescription.
sources.limitations: Guideline states that exercise and several other nonoperative modalities do not improve long-term patient-reported outcomes, based on limited evidence. Its long-term endpoint should not be rewritten as proof of short-term inefficacy or harm. It does not supply a universal gym-exercise contraindication, maximum wrist angle or safe load. Exercise must not be presented as treatment for progressive/severe compression or as a substitute for evaluation. No exercise prescription is extracted from this recommendation.

sources.population: Mild idiopathic CTS,13 men/67 women among completers
sources.comparator: Splint plus median-nerve/tendon glides versus splint alone
sources.coInterventions: Night splint, daytime as needed in both arms
sources.outcomes: No between-group symptom/function/grip/pinch advantage; within-group gains cannot prove added benefit.
sources.uncertainty: Repeated fulltext challenges; AAOS appendix gives3×daily,10reps,5second holds, but secondary dose not accepted as verified primary protocol.
sources.limitations: 80 mild idiopathic CTS patients completed splint+median nerve/tendon glides versus splint alone over 6 weeks. Splints at night, daytime as needed. No significant between-group difference in symptom/function scores, grip or pinch; within-group improvement cannot establish added glide benefit. AAOS evidence appendix reports exercise 3 times/day, 10 repetitions, each position held 5 seconds; dose is secondary extraction, not independently verified methods. Harms not established by the accessible abstract. This is a limited glide candidate, not default treatment for severe CTS, another nerve diagnosis, or postoperative CTS.

Improvement occurred across combinations; no untreated or orthosis-only comparator isolates stretching. At 24 weeks, 25.5% progressed to surgery without group difference. CPG reports no adverse effects. Stretch frequency/hold details in tertiary reports were not accepted as verified primary dosing. This supports cautious selected-population consideration, not a general stretching mandate.

sources.title: Correlation of Segmental Carpal Tunnel Pressures with Changes in Hand and Wrist Positions in Patients with Carpal Tunnel Syndrome and Controls
sources.publicationStatus: Final primary study, Journal of Hand Surgery European Volume 1998;23(5):598–602.

access.details: Primary abstract and/or indexed source passages inspected; complete article inspection not established. Protocol fields deliberately not populated. [Primary abstract](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1016/S0266-7681%2898%2980009-0). DOI 10.1016/S0266-7681(98)80009-0. 39 CTS patients/12 controls; measured pressure at 1-cm intervals in relaxed/gripping hands across neutral/flexed/extended wrists. Patient pressures exceeded controls; relaxed neutral generally lower, extension often higher than flexion. Position, grip and measurement location interacted; simple universal pressure rules are inappropriate. Mechanistic study, no workout intervention, clinical follow-up or safe angle/load endpoint. Supports exploring a symptom-tolerable wrist position, not declaring all loaded wrist extension harmful.
